competences: The learner identifies facts about qualities of a good leader.
The learner states responsibilities and qualities of leaders in the district.
languageCompetence: Pronounce, read and spell district, leader, officer, responsibility, appointment and service.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should identify the key points about qualities of a good leader.
By the end of the lesson learners should answer five original district-leadership questions.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied district leaders, local councils and the services provided by appointed officials.
materials: Chart of district leaders and their duties
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces qualities of a good leader and asks "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader." to recall prior knowledge. They collect learners' responses and relate them to district leadership.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall earlier work on political and civic leaders, answer the starter question and name a district official.

steps.stage: Development: Qualities of a good leader
steps.content: A good leader should be able and competent. A good leader should be kind to others. A good leader should respect other people. A good leader should be knowledgeable. A good leader should be approachable. A good leader should be responsible. A good leader should be hardworking.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on qualities of a good leader, starting with "A good leader should be able and competent. A good leader should be kind to others." They check knowledge using the original question "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders." and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Other qualities expected from leaders
steps.content: A good leader should be tolerant. A good leader should obey lawful instructions. A good leader should be careful. A good leader should cooperate with others. A good leader should set a good example. A good leader should be confident.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on other qualities expected from leaders, starting with "A good leader should be tolerant. A good leader should obey lawful instructions." They check knowledge using the original question "1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong." and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Ways in which leaders attain authority
steps.content: Political leaders gain office through elections. Civic leaders gain office through appointment. Cultural leaders may gain office through inheritance. Voluntary leaders offer service through volunteering. Religious leaders serve their faith communities. Different types of leaders have different responsibilities.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on ways in which leaders attain authority, starting with "Political leaders gain office through elections. Civic leaders gain office through appointment." They check knowledge using the original question "2. Apart from the kings, mention any two other examples of cultural leaders in your" and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.content: Good leaders help settle community disputes. Good leaders help maintain law and order. Good leaders plan community development. Good leaders promote unity among people. Good leaders implement government policies. Good leaders protect people and property.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the source-grounded points on why good leadership matters, starting with "Good leaders help settle community disputes. Good leaders help maintain law and order." They check knowledge using the original question "6. What title is given to a person n who heads a chiefdom?" and explain corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the relevant officials or leadership qualities, answer questions, and copy correct points into their books.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the supplied questions, beginning with "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader." and "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders.". They monitor learners' written answers, then mark and explain them using the reference notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions individually, consult the notes and correct their written responses after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks understanding with "1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong." and "2. Apart from the kings, mention any two other examples of cultural leaders in your". They review the relevant factual points and assign the final question for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state an important point and record the sourced homework question.

assessment: Check the original questions "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader.", "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders.", and "1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong."; mark against the sourced facts.
homework: Complete the original question "6. What title is given to a person n who heads a chiefdom?"
